html:
Artsakh is the old Armenian name for the mountains of Karabakh, between the Kura and Araxes rivers in the southern Caucasus. In 1100, when this map shows it, it was ruled by Armenian princes of Khachen.

In antiquity Artsakh was a province of the kingdom of Armenia, and later passed to Caucasian Albania. In the Middle Ages Armenian princely families held it from mountain fortresses, while the lowland of Arran below was ruled by Muslim emirs. The Principality of Khachen was the main power. In the 13th century, under Prince Hasan-Jalal, the monastery of Gandzasar was built; nearby Dadivank is older.

Its neighbour to the west was Syunik. The region's mixed history lay behind the 20th and 21st century conflict over Nagorno-Karabakh.
